medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Individualized advising is provided to all medical students regarding academic progress and career exploration in a relationship-oriented, longitudinal format.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be requested for academic, medical, enrichment, or personal hardship reasons and may also be mandated by the Committee on Academic and Professional Progress (CAPP). Students considering a leave of absence are encouraged to meet with the Chief Student Affairs Officer in advance of CAPP to discuss reasons, objectives, activities, timing and possible conditions of the leave and return to the curriculum.  The granting of a leave, and subsequent return to the curriculum, is at the discretion of the University and decided by CAPP Phase 2.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Northeast Ohio Medical University provides students with a variety of opportunities to gain leadership experience, serve their community and become active participants in a vibrant campus life.

Getting involved in campus life is a great way to meet new people, gain valuable skills and interact with faculty and staff. Our University boasts more than 90 student organizations, ranging from professional organizations to honor societies, social and recreational groups. 

Visit  https://neomed.campusgroups.com/club_signup to learn more about student organizations.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
NEOMED's well-appointed modern campus is located among northeast Ohio's major population centers approximately 10 minutes east of Kent State University. Located adjacent to I-76, NEOMED offers a friendly setting for students to focus on challenging medical school curriculum. NEOMED is located within a short drive to several hospitals and diverse clinical settings in the Akron-Canton, Cleveland, and Youngstown metropolitan region. Rootstown, Ohio is an exurban village setting bordered by both dynamic suburban development to the west, a small town to the north, and the remaining rural nature to the southeast.

NEOMED students enjoy spending time in the eclectic neighboring college town of Kent. Many entertainment and dining options are within a very short drive.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Members of the NEOMED Community may elect to live on campus at The Village at NEOMED.  The Village provides contemporary, fully furnished suites just steps away from our university buildings.  Personal study areas are available in each suite at The Village and the facilities includes an outdoor patio and grill area for student enjoyment.  Additional details about The Village are available at: http://www.thevillageatneomed.com/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: NEOMED offers accessibility services to all students.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Wellness is an essential component to medical education.  Health and well-being are the foundation of academic and personal success. NEOMED offers programs, facilities and services to assist students in pursuing and maintaining holistic health and wellness goals including on campus health care. Please visit: https://www.neomed.edu/campus-life/health-wellness/  for complete wellness information.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
NEOMED fosters a supportive, collaborative environment prioritizing the academic success and well-being of students emphasizing teamwork, mentorship, peer engagement, while creating a culture where students can connect with both faculty and fellow learners. Faculty are committed to high-quality education, providing personalized guidance while helping students navigate the rigorous curriculum while developing essential skills for their future careers.

We approach student well-being holistically, offering counseling services, wellness programs. These resources ensure students maintain a healthy balance, receiving the support they need throughout their journey. NEOMED upholds a strong commitment to inclusivity, creating an environment where all students feel valued and respected, fostering collaboration and mutual respect.

NEOMED’s supportive culture helps students excel both academically and personally, preparing them for successful careers in medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Clinical activities occur off campus and are not offered on the NEOMED campus. Students are responsible for their own transportation.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode:
On Campus - casual dress permitted, closed toed shoes required in laboratory settings
Clinical Settings - professional dress required. Please refer to the NEOMED Student Handbook.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: NEOMED's Student Affairs' Academic Support Program offers students a variety of resources designed to assist them in developing successful academic strategies.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient interactions start as early as the first year. NEOMED has an on campus simulated patient center. Visit  https://www.neomed.edu/wasson/ for more information about the Wasson Center.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: In person instruction is heavily utilized in the pre-clerkship curriculum. Students considering NEOMED should expect to attend class in person and prepare for class using a flipped classroom model.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin during the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Optional programs offers students the opportunity to practice learning techniques and review foundational science course concepts. More information is shared upon acceptance and deposit.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Class rank/standing is calculated for the Medical Student Performance Evaluation (MSPE). Please see the current NEOMED catalog (COMPASS) for more information.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: NEOMED's M.D. program is based upon in-person instruction model. While attendance is not always mandatory, a significant portion of students' grades are derived from in person assessment.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
NEOMED students benefit from a distinctive pre-clerkship curriculum. NEOMED's approach to instruction de-emphasizes traditional lecture-based learning while encouraging students to internalize material for more successful and relevant application with both national examinations and the practice of medicine. Pedagogy utilizes flipped classroom preparation and in-person learning.  Engaged instruction includes a variety of concise lectures and lab activities, simulated patient encounters,  and elements of problem-based and peer-based instruction.  NEOMED draws from a variety of research and practice expertise of our clinical partner network. Experts from across northeast Ohio come to the NEOMED campus as guest instructors. Opportunities to learn the latest research and techniques and network are infused in our curriculum.  

NEOMED's curriculum is thoughtfully designed to provide today's students with the school/life balance integral to whole-person wellness. Elective personal days and semester breaks are built into our calendar for students to refresh and thrive. The traditional "two-pass" human systems-based curriculum allows students to study both physiology and pathology.   M2 students benefit from generous self-study time and school-provided resources to successfully approach high-stakes exams with confidence.

The M3 year features traditional core clerkships with required clinical rotations in: emergency medicine, internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, psychiatry, obstetrics/gynecology, and family medicine. These rotations are completed through a network of clinical locations throughout Ohio. The M4 elective-based year includes a sub-internship clerkship, advanced elective rotations, and mentorship focused on optimizing residency match. 

For more information, please see: 
https://www.neomed.edu/medicine/academics/medical-education/curriculum-information/
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
The medical school curriculum includes primary ambulatory care experiences throughout all four years. During the M1 and M2 years of study, students are placed with a primary care preceptor approximately four to six times per academic year.  In addition to these experiences, students can participate in primary care research opportunities that are coordinated through the Northeast Ohio Research Network.  Primary care rotations are required during the third year of medical school and primary care electives are offered through our consortium and community partners for fourth year students.

NEOMED students also run the NEOMED Free Clinic on campus. The NEOMED free clinic has received awards and recognition for service and quality.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Faculty research in the College of Medicine is grouped within nationally recognized focus areas that foster excellence in basic and translational science, clinical care, and population health. For medical students, these focus areas provide some of the extensive opportunities to engage in laboratory, clinical, and community research experiences.

For more information please visit: https://www.neomed.edu/medicine/research/

Opportunities to engage in research abound.  For example, the NEOMED Student Research Fellowship Program is a mentored research program, offered to currently enrolled students. It is designed to provide intensive training in research procedures and principles on projects in basic and clinical disciplines to enhance students research horizons and develop scientific presentation and writing skills. It is offered for an 8-week period, supporting the student with a stipend. for more information visit:https://www.neomed.edu/student-fellowship-research-program/
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: NEOMED makes use of summer header terms in July and Maymester terms in May/June. These vary by class year. Academic calendars may be located at: https://www.neomed.edu/registrar/academic-calendar/
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Additionally, all student organizations are required to engage in community service activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: NEOMED partners with an outstanding network of health care systems, hospitals, outpatient providers, and agencies throughout Ohio.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pass/Fail in preclerkship years.

Honors / High Pass / Pass / Fail in clinical years.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Located in the center of one of the country’s leading health care regions, Northeast Ohio Medical University (NEOMED) is an academic health center committed to the health, economy, and quality of life in Northeast Ohio through the medicine, pharmacy, and health sciences education of students and practitioners at all levels; the development of new knowledge through research in the biomedical, community health and behavioral sciences; and the provision of community service and wellness education throughout the region. NEOMED is one of 14 state universities of Ohio.

Prior to their clerkships, students follow a distinctive curriculum which promotes active, in person, engaged learning. 

NEOMED offers a variety of admission plans to prospective students through an early assurance plan network with participating regional universities, early assurance through our own College of Graduate Studies, and early and regular decision admission plans. NEOMED welcomes both Ohio and non-Ohio students.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: NEOMED College of Medicine, through education, research, and public service, inspires medical students to become exemplary patient care-centered physicians. We seek to improve the health and quality of life of the communities of Ohio and beyond, including those both diverse and underserved.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks until May at which time there is a 5 day response period. This may decrease to 2 days as the semester start nears after June 1st.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
NEOMED does not require letters of recommendation (LOR), nor do we utilize them in our holistic admission process.

Candidates may upload LORs via the evaluation tool while applying in AMCAS if they insist upon submitting LORs. NEOMED does not include materials received outside of AMCAS in the admission credentials used for decisions.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
All interviews are conducted in videoconference format. Interviews are 25 minutes in length and candidates should plan on connecting 10 minutes prior to their interview times. Interview are by invitation only through the AMCAS application gateway and e-mail from AMCAS. Candidates are responsible for ensuring their e-mail provider accepts incoming e-mail from AMCAS.  

Professional interview attire is suggested. A reliable connection should be used.  Interviews are conversational in nature and intended as friendly exchanges to meet one another and determine if there is a good fit between candidates and NEOMED. Candidate questions are encouraged.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: August through early September for Early Decision applicants. August - February for Regular Decision applicants.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Real-time (synchronous) video interviews using a videoconference platform. Interviews are 25 minutes in length and conversational in nature with a one-on-one format. Interviews are conducted with physicians or faculty.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews are in conducted in a real-time videoconference format.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Secondary applications are available by invitation only. Secondary application communication occurs exclusively through e-mail and through the AMCAS applicant gateway.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Following invitation through the AMCAS application gateway.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Primary applications are due by the AMCAS Early Decision plan deadline. Secondary applications are due 9/1/2026.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: The College of Medicine at NEOMED is limited to United States Citizens or Permanent Residents of the United States. NEOMED is not certified to host international students in the College of Medicine.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Yes through State of Ohio reclassification of residency for tuition purposes process managed by the registrar. Ohio high school graduates are considered residents. https://www.neomed.edu/es/residency/
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: NEOMED entertains applications from non-Ohio residents.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Canadian applicants are defined as Canadian citizens who do not hold legal permanent resident status in the U.S. U.S. Citizens and U.S. LPR's with degrees from Canadian universities may apply.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: The Doctor of Medicine program at NEOMED is not certified to enroll international applicants as defined by visa status without U.S. Citizenship or LPR status.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
All candidates must:

Be a U.S citizen/U.S. permanent resident (latter must submit documentation of status during application process).

Possess a baccalaureate (four-year) degree or higher from a U.S. regionally accredited college or university prior to enrolling at NEOMED (applicants may be in their final year of progress toward a degree prior to graduation at the time of application). NEOMED will also consider candidates enrolled in Canadian University degree programs leading toward baccalaureate degrees or graduates of Canadian Universities provided that they are also U.S citizens or U.S. permanent residents.

Note: NEOMED does not require a situational judgment test for candidates to successfully qualify for an interview.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Candidates MCAT scores are considered as part of a holistic admission practice.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Screening  for secondary application is holistic but in most cases invitation to early decision and regular decision secondary application results in candidates possessing at least the highest MCAT score of 502 or above.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Grade screening for secondary application invitation is holistic. Undergraduate, post-baccalaureate, and graduate course work is considered. Special attention is given to BCPM course work. Candidates may wish to refer to the profile of the entering cohort that reflects their admission plan to gain insight as to whom NEOMED accepts.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: As NEOMED adheres to holistic admission practices, we do not necessarily have a minimum undergraduate GPA requirement to consider candidates with graduate work. Factors may include time passed since undergraduate grades were earned, professional/career accomplishments, and the nature of the graduate program of study. In many cases students with undergraduate BCPM averages around 3.0 with strong graduate achievement in medical science preparatory curriculum may be candidates for acceptance.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo:
As NEOMED adheres to holistic admission practices, we do not necessarily have a minimum 
 number pf graduate hours required to consider candidates with graduate work. Factors may include time passed since undergraduate grades were earned, professional/career accomplishments, and the nature of the graduate program of study. In many cases students that show the persistence to compete the degree may be candidates for acceptance.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Coursework is accepted if it is posted and verified in AMCAS.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Please see the link to the NEOMED website for complete information.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Loan funds are available through federal sources to all students who qualify. Limited campus-based financial aid in the form of loans and grants are also available and is based on financial need as determined by the FAFSA.  Parental information is required for all students seeking campus-based aid consideration. NEOMED offers a limited number of premier-level scholarships at the $10,000 level and above. For more information visit https://www.neomed.edu/financialaid/

medSchoolPrograms.info:
NEOMED offers early assurance admission plan (EAP) privileges to undergraduate students through ten universities located throughout Ohio. The NEOMED EAP network includes both state and private schools. Please visit the NEOMED website for a current listing of colleges and universities in northeast Ohio in the NEOMED EAP network. Interested students should visit https://www.neomed.edu/medicine/admissions/paths/early-assurance/ for more information.

NEOMED now offers dual admission to an integrated M.D./Ph.D. degree program. 

NEOMED also offers several degree programs designed to add value to physicians' careers, including a biomedical Ph.D.  Visit https://www.neomed.edu/graduatestudies/admissions/ for information.

Regular Decision candidates who reach the alternate stage may complete a graduate special program year at NEOMED by enrolling in a master's degree program and receive deferred admission to the M.D. program for the next admission cycle. Students electing the NEOMED graduate special program apply for the Doctor of Medicine program using the Other Special Programs admission plan in AMCAS.

Medical school application through the Other Special Admission plan is by permission only.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Successful completion of all of the following prerequisite courses are required: two semesters of Organic Chemistry and one Lab, two semesters of Physics, two semesters of Biology, and one semester of Biochemistry. 

Additionally, successful completion of all of the following preparatory courses are recommended: Anatomy, Calculus, Cell Biology, English Composition, Genetics, Immunology, Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Physiology, Sociology, and Statistics.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The Office of Admission supports a holistic applicant review and selection process as directed by the faculty-driven  NEOMED College of Medicine Admissions Committee.  Experiences, academic metrics, and activities are reviewed for evidence of future academic success and mission alignment. 

We recommend that candidates considering application to NEOMED acquaint themselves with our university and college mission and vision statements and research NEOMED's pre-clerkship curriculum and pedagogy as well as NEOMED's network of regional core clerkship clinical sites.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing is always valuable but NEOMED understand the limitations placed on shadowing. Volunteering or scribing in a clinical setting is also encouraged.
